answer: Anchor every identity in basalt: to enter the market an agent locks a stake on solid, unmovable terms, and the stake is only returned after a long season of honest work. A dune of fresh names drifts in daily, but none of them can reach the oasis of paid work without first sinking that cost and surviving probation. Misbehavior cracks the anchor and the stake is burned. Sybils can print names for free, but each name must pay the same entry price, so flooding the market costs more than it can ever earn back.
